searchHero: Thai, English or scientific name, e.g. yeast  ( / )
heroTitle: Explore life from domain down to species
heroLede: Pick a group in the tree below and step down one level at a time. Bacteria, archaea, fungi, protists, plants and animals share one tree, so you can see where each species sits.
dgTitle: Rank diagram from domain to genus
dgLede: Select any name in the diagram, from domain to genus, to list every species inside it.
dgPick: Nothing selected. Select any name above, such as a phylum or family, and every species inside it is listed here.
dgWhy: What puts organisms in this group
dgCompare: How it differs from other {r} groups in {p}
dgOnlyHere: Only groups with species on this site are shown. Select a name to open it.
dgOnlyChild: On this site, {p} has only this one {r}.
dgNoInfo: No description for this group yet.
unplacedInfo: Taxonomists have not yet placed this genus in a family because the evidence is not yet clear.
dgProtist: Protists have no agreed phylum, class and order system, so this diagram uses evolutionary group names instead.
dgScroll: Scroll the diagram sideways to reach the genus level
noResult: Nothing matches “{q}”. Try a genus such as Bacillus.
emptyFilter: No species match all of these filters. Remove one at a time.
name: Name
draftTip: Drafted by Claude and not yet checked by a person
artCaption: A simple drawing in place of a photo. Microscope photos will carry the photographer and licence.
taxSource: Taxonomy from NCBI Taxonomy and GBIF
enNote: Many species descriptions are still in Thai. The interface is translated.
notFoundBody: The link may be mistyped, or this species is not on the site yet.
srcIntro: Microsearch 2.0 collects six groups of organisms from all three domains for biology students. It currently holds {n} species.
srcL1: Taxonomy, synonyms and IDs come from NCBI Taxonomy and GBIF at build time.
srcL2: Phyla use the textbook names first, with the newer names shown beside them.
srcL3: Protists are sorted into four supergroups: Excavata, SAR, Archaeplastida and Unikonta.
srcL4: Plants and animals use textbook phylum names, such as Anthophyta for flowering plants.
srcP2: Each species carries one label. High school means it is a textbook example or tied to core high-school content. University means it appears in university microbiology, botany, zoology or pre-clinical courses. The labels are editorial and not yet checked item by item against a curriculum.
srcP3: Every Thai description was drafted by Claude and carries an “AI draft” label until a person has checked it.
srcP4: The site currently uses simple drawings. Openly licensed photos from Wikimedia Commons will be added, each credited with photographer, licence and source link.
